CVE-2026-102664.title: ProxySQL: Uninitialized heap read in MySQL compressed packet decompression via zlib path
CVE-2026-102664.description: ProxySQL is a proxy for MySQL and its forks, as well as PostgreSQL. Prior to 3.0.10, 3.1.10, and 4.0.10, decompress_mysql_payload() in lib/mysql_data_stream.cpp accepts a zlib stream when uncompress() returns Z_OK without checking that the actual output length equals the attacker-controlled payload_length. An authenticated MySQL client that negotiates compression can overstate payload_length, causing buffer2array() to parse the uninitialized tail of a heap buffer as MySQL packet headers and forward stale data to the backend. Backend error responses can disclose prior SQL queries, result data, credentials, or session state, and malformed lengths can also cause excessive allocations. This issue is fixed in versions 3.0.10, 3.1.10, and 4.0.10.

CVE-2026-118515.description:
The Symfony Serializer component DataUriNormalizer handles only the exact types SplFileInfo, SplFileObject, and File, so for a property typed with a subclass such as UploadedFile, ObjectNormalizer instantiates the object through its constructor from attacker-controlled data, including the file path. This allows an arbitrary file on the server to be treated as an uploaded file in Symfony versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11.

A request body such as {"image": {"path": "/path/to/project/.env.local", "originalName": "a.png", "test": true}} makes the application handle any file on the server as an upload, without the file being sent. With test: true, UploadedFile::isValid() skips is_uploaded_file() and move() falls back to rename(). Assert\File does not prevent this because it validates the file at the attacker-chosen path, which exists on the server.

CVE-2026-97847.description: A flaw was found in the protocol mapper and identity resolution components of Keycloak. The issue occurs when a client manager uses hardcoded-claim mappers to override identity claims in sessionless service-account tokens. Because these tokens lack a session ID, Keycloak may incorrectly resolve the token bearer as a different, highly privileged user based on the manipulated claims. This can allow an attacker with limited client management permissions to impersonate a realm administrator and gain full control over the realm.

CVE-2026-99034.title: mmc: sdhci-sprd: disable runtime PM on remove
CVE-2026-99034.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mmc: sdhci-sprd: disable runtime PM on remove

sdhci_sprd_probe() enables runtime PM, while sdhci_sprd_remove() does
not perform the corresponding runtime PM cleanup.

The probe failure path disables runtime PM before disabling the clocks,
but the normal remove path directly disables clocks that are also
managed by the runtime PM callbacks. If the device is runtime
suspended, those clocks may already be disabled.

Resume the device before removal, disable runtime PM and drop the
temporary runtime PM reference before disabling the clocks.

This issue was found by manual code inspection.

CVE-2026-99041.title: ip6_gre: remove obsolete ERSPAN PMTU update
CVE-2026-99041.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ip6_gre: remove obsolete ERSPAN PMTU update

A tc tunnel_key action can attach a METADATA_IP_TUNNEL dst to an skb,
and mirred can redirect it to a native ip6erspan device. The legacy PMTU
update in ip6erspan_tunnel_xmit() treats that metadata dst as a route.
Since it has no output device, dst_dev(dst)->mtu dereferences NULL.

On v7.2 with KASAN, an initial UID/GID 65534 process with CapEff 0 used
self-created user and network namespaces to trigger:

KASAN: null-ptr-deref
RIP: ip6erspan_tunnel_xmit+0x10fc/0x2cc0
Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt

The update is obsolete. Commit fe1a4ca0a2b7 ("ip6_gre: process toobig
in a better way") changed IPv6 GRE Too Big handling to update the
underlay route and removed the equivalent block from __gre6_xmit().
ip6_tnl_xmit() then propagates the underlay PMTU to the overlay route.

Remove the stale ERSPAN copy and its now-unused dst variable. This
eliminates…

CVE-2026-99148.title: drm/amdgpu: keep the eviction fence until the last handle is closed
CVE-2026-99148.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdgpu: keep the eviction fence until the last handle is closed

amdgpu_gem_object_close() detaches the user queue eviction fence from
the BO before it checks bo_va->ref_count, so closing any handle of a BO
removes the fence, even when the file still has another handle to the
BO and the bo_va with its GPU mappings stays. The BO can then be evicted
without suspending the user queues of the file, which keep accessing it
through mappings that are only marked for update.

Seen on navi31 with a SDMA user queue: a BO opened twice in the same
file (GEM_FLINK + GEM_OPEN) loses its eviction fence when the second
handle is closed (traced attach/detach of the fence):

attach bo=ffff8c78a6c84c00
GEM_CLOSE handle=7
detach bo=ffff8c78a6c84c00

while handle 6 and the mapping are still in use.

Only detach the fence when the last reference to the bo_va goes away,
matching amdgpu_gem_object_open(), which attaches it only when…

CVE-2026-99409.title: xfs: don't fix the directory tree if live update fails
CVE-2026-99409.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: don't fix the directory tree if live update fails

LOLLM complains that we don't double-check dl->aborted one last time to
before committing repairs to the filesystem. This is important because
the live update handler could have set ->aborted if it encountered a
runtime error.

CVE-2026-99496.title: s390/vmcp: Initialize full session info to zero
CVE-2026-99496.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/vmcp: Initialize full session info to zero

The cma_alloc bit as well as the response can contain old data.
cma_release will not free the kmalloced memory in that case and
the response code might leak kernel stack data to CAP_SYS_ADMIN
users.

CVE-2026-99618.title: nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page
CVE-2026-99618.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet: don't return memory contents beyond valid data when reading ANA log page

The host side does not know how much valid data will be returned by the target
so it will typically provide a buffer larger than the amount of valid data in
the ANA log page. The memory allocation used by the target does not guarantee
that prior kernel memory contents will not be returned past the end of the valid
page data. Fix this to ensure that the SGL is zeroed before copying the data.
